utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Haradinaj, in your absence, the Chamber expressed that it very much regretted the circumstances which led you to apply for provisional release. The Chamber hopes that it has assisted you and your family in overcoming this loss. Then I would like to give some guidance to the parties in respect of the annexes to the 92 ter statement of Zoran Stijovic. The Chamber tries to work as precisely as possible on the matter. The Chamber, which may not be a surprise, sometimes has logistical difficulties also in finding moments to deliberate and to express views internally so as to come to decisions, so therefore I'm not at this moment giving a decision, but I announce that the parties should not be surprised if the following annexes would not be admitted into evidence, and I also can tell you already that this does not cover the whole range. It covers the range up till number 52 on the list of annexes. So therefore the parties should not be surprised if annex 17 and 18 would not be admitted into evidence; if annex 25 would not be admitted into evidence; if 40, 41, 42, and 43 would not be admitted into evidence; if 46 would not be admitted into evidence; and if 49 would not be admitted into evidence. I'm not going to give you at this moment detailed reasons. You may have noticed that reports as such -- DB reports as such are not yet announced as -- to be of no surprise if they would not be admitted into evidence. This can have different kinds of reasons, such as sometimes you find elements in there which corroborate some other evidence or show a certain awareness of events having taken place or still to take place. And therefore admission also doesn't mean that for the content that the Chamber accept that automatically as being true. Furthermore, you -- if you would analyse this announcement in further detail, you might also find that if a statement points at very specific acts of a specific accused, that the Chamber apparently hesitates to admit such material into evidence. If you analyse it as well as far as statements given just after the 24th of March, 1998, of -- statements given by persons who were apparently as a result of what happened on the 24th of March detained, that there the Chamber hesitates to admit such statements into evidence. Sometimes also because we have heard a lot of viva voce evidence on what happened on the 24th of March and sometimes there seems to be in the written statements, there seems to be quite some contradiction. This is not full reasons, but it may also guide the parties when considering the remainder of the annexes. Further, I would like to ask you, Mr. Re: Annexes 1 and 26 were related to portions of the 92 ter statements, which have been redacted by now. This is not to say that you could not seek to tender them, but the Chamber just draws your attention that the direct link between the 92 ter statement, which is not the same as the direct link to the evidence given by the witness, but the direct link with the 92 ter statement has gone lost. This, as far as guidance is concerned for the time being. Mr. Re, are you ready to continue the examination-in-chief of the witness? Then, Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Stijovic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And I think there was another matter about the proposal for any decision on the Operation Krug. I think you would look in your hotel room whether you would have it with you. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we were discussing was the Bezbednost magazine. I said that I have that issue. However, I wasn't able to locate it; although, I can tell you that it was issue number 5 for 1998. I have another copy here. It is a professional magazine of the Ministry of the Interior. This copy, however, is from 2005. The one I referred to in my testimony was edition number 5 from 1998. It is a professional magazine that deals with topics of security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I -- I mixed up two matters - that's true - that this is especially the basis for the statistics. Mr. Emmerson, would it assist you if Mr. Stijovic would give it just for the time being so that you can have a look at this 2005 copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My instinctive reaction is no, since it's not the source of the information that the witness quotes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then if any of the other Defence counsel would like to have a look at it, then I'll wait for -- for an application. Mr. Re, are you ready to continue? Then Mr. Re will now continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On Thursday afternoon I was asking you about paragraph 20 of your statement and the statistics you noted there of the number of attacks by separatists between 1992 and 1998, ranging from 8 in 1992 to 1.486 in 1998 through the 30th of November. Just to complete -- I'm sorry, I think someone turned this microphone off and not the other one. I just got the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? Someone did ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just ask whether I can be heard. I have a difficulty with this microphone because it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now they are both switched on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. But this one, the papers rattle right next to it. Someone keeps turning them on and off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I'm not doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the one who does is invited to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question I want to ask you is in relation to the rest paragraph, the part where it goes (a) to (t). Each of those attacks you have outlined there, included in the statistics of the beginning of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On Thursday afternoon you also gave us some evidence about the murder of one Luftu Ajazi in paragraph 19. What was your information at the time as to why he was killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either there was a mistake in interpretation or there is a miscommunication. I wasn't talking about a homicide. I was talking about a terrorist attack on Luftu Ajazi whereby he was seriously wounded. In the interpretation I am receiving, there was a murder that was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My mistake. I meant "attack," as opposed to "murder." What was the information you received at the time about why he was attacked?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luftu Ajazi had worked for a great number of years for the RDB in Kosovo. He was from the area of Drenica, from Glogovac, who was very well acquainted with the functioning of the Albanian extremism and terrorism. Over a period of time --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to object to his answer as being not responsive. The question was: What information did you receive? If he wishes to expand the answer, I have no difficulty with it. But my concerns are since in the absence of knowing the source of the information, this gentleman is going to give us a long lecture with regard to what this particular individual did as a job and we won't get to the ultimate issue, which is information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, to some extent, of course, if you -- if you talk about information you receive about an attack on a certain person, then the position of that person and perhaps specific knowledge he may have had does not exclude from that type of information. But, Mr. Re, at the same time you are invited to elicit from the witness what the source of his information was. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For every question like that, I want you to tell the Trial Chamber - but as briefly as possible - the source of your information. Understand? A moment ago, you were telling us about Mr. --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand the question. I was about to answer. I wanted to explain why he was chosen to be the target. But since you are insisting on the source of information, it was my direct knowledge that I gained in a telephone conversation with his brother immediately after the terrorist attack had been carried out, as well as the information we obtained subsequently through our operational activities concerning that attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's -- that's what I'm interested in, the latter. What was the information you had as to why he was attacked, why he was targeted and attacked? What was the source of that information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The source of information were the people who immediately participated in the work of the terrorist group around Adem Jashari that was located in Prekaze near Srbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were you told or what did you find out?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We obtained some information from our source stating that the terrorist group of Adem Jashari is in possession of lists of people that they are to carry out attacks on in the area of Drenica. In that regard, particular focus was placed on the workers of the police, of the Security Service, as well as Albanians employed by the various bodies of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia. Luftu Ajazi was one of the most competent and highly positioned people in the area of Kosovo within the category mentioned on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was his name on the list?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was your name on the list?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why wasn't your name on the list?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I suppose -- I suppose that Luftu Ajazi's name was on the list because he was from the area. He was a well-known person there, and he directly worked with the People's Movement of Kosovo over a number of years and he -- he had been a year-long employee of the State Security Service. He began working for the RDB in early 1970s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: All right. I've got -- I have a light. I was slow getting to my feet, but the question called for complete speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The answer was pure speculation. And in my submission, Mr. Re didn't need to go there and shouldn't have gone there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I've given that some thought as well, and I wondered how I would have put that question to the witness. I think I would have asked the witness under those circumstances whether he knows of a reason why he was not on the list, as the first question. The answer then most likely would be "no." And then perhaps the next question could have been whether he made any observations as to the composition of those lists. And then he might or might not have said that those on the list were locals and there were -- there was something to explore there which came out into the answer, but I tend to agree with you that the way in which the evidence was elicited was not perfect in terms of trial techniques.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We have a -- we have another problem with the manner which this particular question and answer is proceeding, which is there's an assumption that in fact there is a list, a physical --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, that came into my mind as well, and then it should have said the -- the reported list. Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just getting constant objections. I could have got through this three minutes ago without these objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My next question was going to be: Did you see the list? But I can't get to it because I keep getting interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps -- perhaps if you start with: Have you seen the list? Then you avoid all these objections and then all the thoughts that came into the mind of Defence counsel and some of the thoughts that came into my mind as well, would not have been there. But that's -- as I said before, it's -- it's not dramatic but it's also... Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I simply want to take this moment, if I may, to reiterate as far as this evidence and all subsequent testimony is concerned, the witness is citing a source unnamed and we are assuming without raising objections from here on in at each occasion that where that is the case the source is not -- the witness is unwilling to name the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what we discussed last Thursday. If the witness is in a position to give the name of the source, he's invited to do so. If he doesn't give a name, it is interpreted as the witness having reasons for not using that name. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I still, of course, stand guided by the Trial Chamber, but I can't always ask the questions in the order that other people anticipate that -- I will ask them. I will ask them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, of course not how they anticipate but there is some logic in it. If you start with -- if you wanted to ask whether the witness has seen the list, then before asking explanations on who is on the list and who is not on the list, I think you avoid a lot of problems if you first establish whether he has seen the list so that we know exactly what the basis of his knowledge is as far as who is on the list, who's not on the list, and then next question, why A is on the list and B is not on the list. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, we're talking about this list and I was asking you whether your name was on the list and you said "no." Did Serbian State Security see this list or have a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see the list?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that's the reason why you're able to tell the Trial Chamber that your name wasn't on it, because when you looked at it, you didn't see it there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether the people who compiled the list knew who you were? Given your --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What's the answer to that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. How did Serbian State Security obtain this list?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During 1994, in mid-1994, to be more specific, we carried out an action arresting a broad group of members of the so-called Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Kosovo. And during investigations and the criminal proceedings that were subsequently conducted, we established that the so-called parallel service of the public security service of the Republic of Kosovo made very detailed investigations of the movements, the conduct, and the relationships of members of the SDB in that area; that it revealed or discovered people who were in contact with the DB; and that they got a list or knew of a number of Albanians who had been in the -- in contact with the Serbian RDB. What we discovered as the DB during that investigation was that this parallel service -- this parallel security service --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm really interested in a shortcut answer, as in, like, who gave you the list.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received the list from employees of the State Security Service after searching the apartment of Avdija Mehmetovic, who was at the time the head of the State Security of Kosovo. That was that parallel Albanian Security Service or DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. What happened to the list? Where is it now?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list is in the archives of the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia or in the archives of the BiA [as interpreted] currently and the action in relation to this was an operative action named Zeto [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please turn to paragraph 17 of your statement. And I just inform you the Trial Chamber is not admitting that paragraph into evidence. However, I wish to ask you about the document which is annex 1 -- or referred to annex 1 in that paragraph. It's a LPK public declaration published in Zeri i Kosoves on the 1st of September, 1993. What I want you to do is have a look at the annex and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And for the record, it's P933. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Trial Chamber what the significance of that document was to the State Security when they read it. And while the witness is doing that, can I remind the Trial Chamber that these -- these extracts are from the book that Mr. Jakup Krasniqi brought with him to the Trial Chamber to the -- to the court and the Trial Chamber asked Mr. Krasniqi questions about this book which contains the communique. And that's at pages 5159 to 5160 of the transcript. So every annex of Mr. Stijovic's statement which refers to these communiques from that book, this book, it relates to the book that Mr. Krasniqi brought to the Trial Chamber at the conclusion of his evidence. The question is, Mr. Stijovic: What was the significance to the State Security when they read it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting that was held in August in the area of Drenica LPK was especially significant for us because the results of the meeting were the general commitment of the People's Movement of Kosovo to prepare people for armed actions in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How does that relate to the political declaration in MFI P933?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is directly connected or directly related because the LPK in that political declaration publicly and openly advocated the need to activate or carry out active measures to stand up against the authorities in Serbia, first of all, in terms of armed activities and armed actions in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And where does that fit in in the general transition from the isolated or the eight attacks you've referred to in paragraph 20 leading up to the 75 attacks you've referred to in 1997? Where does this document fit in in that general pattern of increased -- or the increasing attacks over those years?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on even a superficial analysis, it can easily be determined that after this Drenica meeting the activity or the terrorist activities and violence in Kosovo and Metohija registered an increase and the culmination of the activities began from 1995 onwards. From 1995 onwards, you could see a dramatic increase of the attacks, which then escalated in late 1998, which is mentioned in paragraph 20 from -- counting or numbering 1.486 attacks through the 30th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please turn to paragraph 20(b) of your statement. Can that please be displayed in Sanction. Thank you. Ask you referred to KLA communique number 18, that's annex 6 of your statement. What's the exhibit number? It's annex 6. I'm just getting the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar has prepared a -- a list with all the MFI numbers in relation to the annexes. 6 would be P938.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In paragraph 20(b), you refer to: "The synchronised nature of the attacks indicates a significant degree of integration and communication between different KLA groups, even in early 1996." Now, if you can just turn to the communique itself, and in particular the first paragraph. If that could be displayed in e-court. Of -- in the English, where it says communique number 18, the first paragraph on the 11th of February, 1996: "The guerilla units of KLA initiated military actions in operative zone number 1. Actions were carried out using hand-grenades in the camps of Serb colonizers arriving from the Krajina in the capital of the Republic of Kosovo, Pristina, as well as Mitrovica, Peja, Podujevo, Suhareke, and Vushtrri." How do you come to assess those particular attacks as synchronised?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer this very clearly. Self-organising of the actions carried out within ten minutes on a broader area of Kosovo and Metohija indicates that there was a plan and that there was an intention to carry out these actions. It's not easy to carry out so many attacks without good logistics and good preparation. The targets of the attacks were not chosen at random; although, in this case the direct target were the facilities where persons under the protection of the United Nations were located. The actual target of these attacks were the authorities and the message to the authorities was, as you read in the announcement, that those so-called Serbian colonisers should be moved from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. In that sense, the term to take over responsibility used by the KLA in this announcement points to a logical development of events in which way and how they were planning their further activities. After this action and after several more actions, we made the decision, based on analysis, to turn around the operative action, because these attacks and some subsequent attacks that took place at the same time provided us with the absolute right to conclude that they were backed by a well-organised group or organisation that was carrying out these actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can I please -- I know you've -- there's a lot of information you want to tell the Trial Chamber, but can you please try and confine the answer to the question, which was about synchronisation, if possible. My follow-up question in relation to this is - it's on the screen in front of you, it's the first paragraph in communique number 18, and you just referred to "Serb colonisers." Who were these people that the communique is referring to as "Serb colonisers" and what was their significance in terms of the KLA's objectives and the actions they took?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were persons who, as refugees from the territory of the Republic of Croatia, were accommodated in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Also in relation to the so-called Serb colonisers, can you please turn to paragraph 22(e) of your statement. And it refers to KLA communiques. And in particular, number 22, in relation to an attack on three houses in Babaloc. And we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it your reference was to 20(e).

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I do mean 20(e). I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Also because the term "so-called" is actual a term of argument within these proceedings. Within regard to the communique that we're referring to, that particular language,"so-called," does not exist. Mr. Re has just used that language, that "so-called." I just wish for there to be a distinction between who is making a determination about so-called Serb colonisers. And I'm dealing specifically with "so-called"." And this will become self-evident. As a matter of fact, it's one of the issues that was raised in the motion that we filed with regard to this gentleman's testimony in terms of particular terminology that was being used. Since the word "so-called" is being used, I'm alerting the Chamber to that and I just ask that there be some careful use of language here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, "so-called" suggests that the name does not reflect what the object or the person or the group actually is. And at the same time, I see that this is the terminology the witness used in his 92 ter statement, so to that effect it is -- there's no problem if you refer to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's what I did. I'm just referring to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm dealing specifically with -- no, let me just -- let me just check exactly what ... If you would have said also in relation to what you refer to as the "so-called," then it's clear you're referring to what the witness said, rather than you use the term yourself. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And at the same time, I'm saying that I'm displaying it on the screen his statement, in which he says "so-called Serb colonisers." And I'm just referring him to that so I can move to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's all I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, this -- this way of using language might perhaps easily confuse a jury. It certainly will not confuse this Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate that. I just want to make sure we don't have difficulty with it at a later point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Because it will be something in issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, I'm only referring to paragraph 22(e), and you relate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, again, 20(e)?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry, 20 -- 20(e). I saw the words 22 -- sorry, communique 22, paragraph 20(e). And you say: "Attack on three houses in Babaloc in which so-called Serb colonisers (refugees from the Krajina) were being accommodated." Were those people you referred to there as "so-called Serb colonisers" were they in the same category as the Serbian refugees you referred to a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before the witness answers, annex 10 is the source of this paragraph, and the relevant provision in annex 10 refers to an attack not on houses in which refugees were being accommodated but on apartments that were in the process of being constructed. In other words, on a building site.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. But I'm sure the appropriate submission can be made at the appropriate time or questions asked in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there are two matters. The first is that references should be as precise as possible already in chief and not only corrected in cross-examination. And at the same time, whether the houses were meant to be used for accommodation of so-called colonisers and they're under construction or whether already used, I wouldn't say it makes no difference but --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It is simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The difference is limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The question is being asked about people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- who were accommodated within those buildings. That -- that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, no, that's not true either, Mr. Emmerson. And it was an attack on three houses. It's not an attack on individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is still -- the object is the house. But let's try to avoid to spend hours and hours on what may be not an important but still details and not -- certainly not the main matters with which this Chamber is concerned. Please proceed, Mr. Re. So therefore I -- the Defence is invited to save -- I think in the song it's save it for a rainy day. That's too long, but at least save it for a while and not to interrupt and -- the flow of evidence again and again. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In respect to the last objection, can I remind the Trial Chamber - and, of course, Mr. Emmerson - I'm sure he's aware of this - that annex 3 to Mr. Jakup Krasniqi's Rule 92 ter statement - that's Exhibit P328 - is a report of that very attack and it's been tendered into evidence and it refers to an -- quote -- "An attack at a settlement of Serb and Montenegrin refugees at Babaloc village of Decan." And that is -- and that is a KLA communique which has been published in Pristina Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It still doesn't resolve the matter on whether these houses were at that moment inhabited by persons or not yet. And as I said before, details of minor importance. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to take you to -- I'm sorry. Excuse me for a moment I just want the question. I was asking you about the attack on that particular settlement, whether the houses were being built or not. Were they the same types of refugees that you were referring to a little earlier?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not. This settlement - and perhaps it will help if I clarify the situation for the Trial Chamber - the settlement of Babaloc was a specific settlement with a large number of houses where Serbs and Montenegrins who had fled from Albania, who had come as refugees, were supposed to be accommodated. This was financed with UNHCR funds. And as the houses were being completed, people were moving in. There were scores of houses there. It was a restricted area or smaller area where those houses were located. And as the houses were completed, people were moving in. Everybody in the area knew that it was a settlement where refugees from Serbia and Montenegro were accommodated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Also in relation -- in that particular KLA communique, which was number 22, can you please look at the first paragraph, in which it said: "As stated in the communique, number 22 on July 7th and 10th, KLA has executed two attempted attacks. The first attack was carried out on the collaborator of the Serb regime, Shukri Krasniqi from Ostrozubi, and the second one in Podujevo on the criminal Sredoje Radojevic"? Did you have any information at the time about those particular attacks, that is, the collaborator and the police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Shukri Krasniqi was killed at a catering facility, and our subsequent information that we gained during our investigations was that among the three people who had killed Shukri Krasniqi included Fatmir Limaj. As for Radojevic, the police officer we know reliably that the executor was Jasir Barasiti [phoen], called Vuk, Wolf, who was leading the KLA activities in the areas of Lab and Podujeve.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was Shukri Krasniqi, referred to as a collaborator in this KLA communication?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have specific information about who he was, other than this was a person who had been seen with members of the police, and it's possible that that was the criteria on the basis of which he was picked as a target.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The person called Wolf, who was leading the KLA activities in Lab and Podujevo, does he have a name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has begun to rain. You said save it for a rainy day. But it is pouring at the moment. This is -- again, we have no idea what the sources of this information are, what the relevance of any of this information is to this witness's testimony is -- is really getting very far afield, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, as far as sources are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I do intend to cover it. I mean, an objection is not going to make me do it any faster. Before I move away from this document, I will cover that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The other issue is -- I've asked that myself -- what level of detail we will need where it apparently seems to -- that you want to establish that already quite a few events happened years before the year of the indictment which were related to KLA and which are covered by KLA communiques. The level of detail of that material, of course, is -- as needed is questionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It goes, of course, to the reliability or the accuracy of the matters contained in those KLA communiques. The Trial Chamber has heard evidence from Mr. Krasniqi as to the fact that they were disseminated. And the Defence of Mr. Haradinaj has specifically objected or has -- has said they question or object to the Prosecution attempting to tender them for the truth of the contents. Mr. Stijovic is well-placed to give evidence of the truth of the contents and to verify the accuracy of each of the KLA communiques which are annexed to his statement. And the significance of the KLA communiques shows the escalation of the KLA activities against Serbian collaborators and police officers until it escalated into an armed conflict during the indictment period. So it's highly relevant to show the buildup and how it came to turn from terrorist attacks upon collaborators and police to a -- an armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, the Chamber understands that on the basis of the objections made, as far as the content of this material is concerned, that you spent some time on it, but the level of detail could be really limited. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey was interested, over there, in the source of your information in relation to the attacks on Shukri Krasniqi and the police officer Mr. Radojevic. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber as briefly as you possibly can where the DB or the MUP obtained its information about what happened?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By carrying -- or by intercepting a group of the LPK people, including the brother of Fatmir Limaj and a series of other persons who had been included in this activity. This is in terms of Shukri Krasniqi. As for Sredoje Radojevic, through our associate we found out about a person who was carrying out attacks in the Podujevo area. We received a phone number and a pseudonym that he used in telephone communications. And that pseudonym was Vuk, Wolf. An example of the measures we used was bugging. Then we determined that that person was a key person for the execution of terrorist attack in -- attacks in the area of Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you have a name for Wolf?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zahir Pajaziti.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you assess the reliability of the information you obtained at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By combining the technical means at our disposal and the human sources I discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why was it so reliable?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the source that informed us about the murder of Sredoje Radojevic was a person who was in close contact with the late Pajaziti, Zahir. And if I may, I would like to explain something, however I would like to do it in private session when stating where that person was at the time so as not to put him in any danger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session. Then we have to -- since we're in Courtroom II now, we have to move the curtains down as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please turn to paragraph 20(h) of your statement, in which you refer to the serious wounding of the dean of the University of Pristina, Radivoje Papovic, on the 16th of January, 1997. And it appears in KLA communique number 29, which is annex 13, MFI P946. In your statement, you note that the KLA has taken responsibility for that particular -- I'm sorry, if I said "946", I meant 945. I just correct that. What was your information in January 1997 - I'm displaying the relevant portion of communique number 29 in Sanction - as to the collaborationist -- I'm sorry, as to why Radivoje Papovic was attacked by the KLA. He is described there as an enemy of the people. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radivoje Papovic was a professor at the University of Pristina and also the dean of the university. In addition to that, he was a well-known figure, and as such he often openly discussed the situation in Kosovo and Metohija. Since he was well acquainted with the situation and the continuity of operation of Albanian separatists, he was able to clearly define their true intentions and goals. In that regard, in the Albanian media he was presented as a hard-liner among the Serbs. He was often the target of many attacks -- verbal attacks. And as we can see here, a physical attack followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he a civilian?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. A professor at the school of mathematics and natural sciences. I think he specialised in chemistry. He had a Ph.D. A well-known person, an influential figure among the Serbian population in the area of Kosovo-Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How does the information the DB had compare with the information in communique number 29 published by the KLA on the 19th of January, 1997? I mean, what I'm asking you is: The KLA communique, does it reflect what happened?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It compares absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one in that communique refers to the third attack. "The third attack targeted the collaborator of the Serbs, Xun Dervishi from Skenderaj"? What information did you have in particular about that attack? Just very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The RDB, a few hours after the attack, learned of the event. We quickly put two and two together. We followed the sequence of events and the behaviour of those who we were monitoring, realising that the terrorist group from Prekaze was behind the attack in its wider composition, that the attack was carried out by the members of the group surrounding Adem Jashari in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber also wants the know the source of the information. Where did the DB get its sources from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sources were first and foremost -- well, I can mention pseudonyms, if it is of any importance to the Chamber. I can mention the pseudonyms of our live sources who were positioned highly within the terrorist nucleus in Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you telling the Trial Chamber that highly placed sources within the KLA provided you with information about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people were very close to the innermost leadership of the KLA. I think that would be a precise way of putting it. They were active members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would revealing pseudonyms endanger these people if it were done in open session?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not, since that associate of the RDB after 1999 was compromised. Certain members of the KLA and NPK learned of his identity. I think I can say what his pseudonym, his first and last name is, and other details. That person, after he was killed in Drenica, received the rank of colonel in the KLA. His pseudonym was Moralec. There was a brigade in the Shala area that was named after him. If you want me, I can state his first and last name, since the -- his award and the name of the brigade had subsequently been changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It cannot do any harm either to him or to his family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it does no harm, you could just give the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mehe Uka. A year-long member of the NPRK, he spent over 15 years in prison. He was also somebody who worked for us and we enlisted him during his prison sentence. Once he was released, he worked within the group of Adem Jashari, as well as the National Movement for the liberation of Kosovo that were led by --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could repeat the two names he mentioned. The interpreter did not hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Through him, we were able to put together our arrest operation very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why was he providing information, this colonel in the KLA, to the Serbian State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was posthumously pronounced general. A KLA brigade got its name after him. The basic reason why Mehe Uka accepted to cooperate with the RDB had to do with his disappointment in the relationship and opportunism that was prevailing at the time among certain members of the KLA. Ideologically speaking, he was a Marxist-Leninist, a hard-liner, and his position was clear. In his interview with us, he told us that he very much disagreed with what was going on in the NPK and he said that that was not what he had opted for at the time he had joined the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did the DB give him in return for his information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, apart from some support, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And how did you assess at the time the reliability of the information he was providing you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was such a reliable associate that I can mention two very good examples which can easily be corroborated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are they referred to in your statement? Do they relate to incidents referred to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If it would assist the Trial Chamber, I can lead the evidence. If the Trial Chamber has a general concern about the reliability of the information the DB was relying upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Oh, there we go. It might insist the Trial Chamber to know whether the Mehe Uka that the witness has just spoken of, is the one who according to a statue that I am looking at courtesy of Mr. and Mrs. Google appears to have died in 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- we are talking about -- first of all, is that -- is that your information as well, that he died in 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. Mehe Uka. Mehe Uka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we see under paragraph 20 a lot of information about early years. So therefore as such, that does not necessarily come as a surprise, because it's not covering the events in 1998. So therefore, Mr. Harvey, I do not know whether your reference to Mr. and Mrs. Google -- what do -- is -- are you suggesting that he could not have given reliable information because he died already before the events happened that he would have given information about? Is that what you suggested?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, I'm not suggesting that. I'm suggesting that -- we've spent a lot of time in 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I'm wondering whether we're going to move on to anything that's really relevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That has got nothing to do with the reliability of this source and that was what was on the table at the time. Mr. Re, the Chamber has no specific concerns about -- Mr. Emmerson -- has no specific concerns about the reliability of the person who died in 1996. Please proceed. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just wonder if it might be clarified. It may be my misunderstanding, but I had thought that this related to information acquired as a source in respect of events taking place in 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have to check that. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It doesn't say that in the communique. The communique was issued on the 19th of 1997, referring to a third attacked target. It doesn't say when they attacked the Serbian collaborator, Mr. Xun Dervishi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In terms of -- in looking at the communique itself, the first attack dates the 13th of January. Then chronologically, the second action dates the 16th of January, and the third attack, which has no date, since it's a third attack, one would think that it would come after that date as a matter of logic and the year would be 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check. Mr. Re, and your chronology following the logic of Mr. Guy-Smith or would you like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- elicit --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have no information in that communique as to the date of the attack on Mr. Xun Dervishi at all. I'm not going to make a submission as to whether it occurred in that month or the month before or whenever.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, again, the -- Messrs. Google insists that the attack on the rector of the university who was also a major leader of the Serb socialist party took place on the -- it was either the 15th or the 16th of January, 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And talking about reliability, you consider Mr. and Mrs. Google a reliable source, Mr. Harvey? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: More so than this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that an admission from the Defence that the KLA attacked and -- attacked the rector of the University of Pristina on the basis he was a Serb collaborator on the 16th of January, 1997?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm not going to sink to this level, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, why simply Google then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, an imperfect attempt to verify certain dates and an imperfect attempt to see whether a person who allegedly has died in 1996 could give any information about an event that may have taken place in 1997, that's the issue we're talking about, reliability of that source and whether the Chamber, not consulting Mr. and Mrs. Google on a frequent basis, had no -- at firsthand, no serious concerns about reliability. Perhaps on the basis of what was put forward again -- again, not as a final answer but as a -- as a -- as an attempt to quickly seek verification of certain data, might require further exploration of the reliability of this source. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Your Honour, may I address you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you -- where you may have noticed that some matters have been raised in relation to who could give information about events that had taken place at a certain time. If -- if you can -- although you are a witness, if you have any matter, to your knowledge, that could assist us in better understanding these documents, you're invited to give that information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we were discussing Zahir Pajaziti, a mentioned a person who was sending us information from the prison, including the phone number and the pseudonym of Vuk, used by Pajaziti. That person, however, was not Mehe Uka. Mehe Uka used the pseudonym Moralec, and he participated in the activities of the KLA and the group of Adem Jashari in Prekaze. He also assisted us in surveying Zahir Pajaziti and it made us possible to confirm that he was the key organiser of the action against Mr. Radojevic. The person who helped us with the latter portion was another person, not Mehe Uka. It was somebody who was also in prison in Serbia. I can tell you what his name was. However, these are two separate people. One of them helped us with the attack on Radivoje Papovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to take you to paragraph 20(o) of your statement. And it refers to communique number 40, which is MFI P953. Mr. Jakup Krasniqi gave evidence in the Limaj trial T33 -- page 3325. It's part of the Limaj testimony which is in -- in evidence here. And it refers to a number of attacks in November 1997 upon various people. And you referred to these in your statement. One of them refers to -- the first one is a -- one Zdravko Tomcic, the communique refers to it as the Serbian-imposed chairman of the commune of Podujeve in Operational Zone number 5. What was the information the DB had at the time about that particular attack and what is meant by "Serbian-imposed chairman of the commune"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll start from the beginning. I believe the person's name was Zdravko; although, I am not 100 per cent certain. He was appointed by the Serbian Assembly to the position of the president of the Municipality of Podujevo since there was a boycott in place on the part of the Albanians from that area, they refused to participate in work with the authorities. He wasn't imposed per se; however, he was placed there in order to ensure the functioning of the local authorities, since the Albanians there did not wish to do that. The assembly had to come up with a decision appointing a person to discharge the tasks envisaged by the law. This was quite a surprise to us, the attack on that person, since his residence was in the municipality of Kursumlija, which is the adjacent municipality of Podujevo. However, the message was a clear one. Be it Kursumlija or anywhere, even the president of the municipality or any other person cannot be safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he a civilian?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the information in this KLA communique, that is, that he was attacked by a hand-grenade, accord with what the DB was informed actually happened?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. The RDB also conducted an on-site investigation, and we found certain pieces of the hand-grenade that was thrown at Mr. Tomcic's family house. There was a complete file in existence concerning this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your statement, you also at paragraph 20(r), 20(s), and 20(t), refer to this same communique in relation to -- Can we have the rest of that page -- In relation to an attack on a colleague of your, Dragan Davidovic, another police officer, Zeljko Lutovac, the murder of Dalup Dugoli, and the claimed shooting down -- or shooting of a Cessna 310 aeroplane at Golesh aerodrome. A general question, to try to move quickly to the point here: How accurate was the information in the KLA communique or how does it compare to the information which the DB had at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards this specific case, it is absolutely incorrect. The quote from item (T) mentions the shooting down of a Cessna 310 aeroplane on the 26th of November, 1998. That is incorrect. It was another thing that appeared regularly in one -- in many communiques by the KLA. They often used propaganda stating that in their actions, in general, they caused or inflicted serious losses to the occupiers and that they withdrew without any consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How much of this particular communique was -- I think you said 20 -- I heard the words 26 November, 1998. Did you say 1998 or 1997 a moment ago? The transcript says "1998".

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1998? It's 1997. However, in this subparagraph the year is wrong. That is what confused me. This was probably a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may take it that a report of December 1997 could not deal with any matter that took place on the -- in November 1998. I further, Mr. Re, I would like to draw your attention that in annex 10 there is a rather confusing typo in the English text. The first communique mentioned there should be 21, as in the original, and not 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll ask for that to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And on the same document that we've just been looking at in subparagraph (s), presumably the same date error applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I assume so, but I can certainly clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would do that and we will then have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to clarify something. The date in paragraph (s), should that be 1997? And the other thing I wanted to ask you was: The accuracy in relation to what you've written in paragraph (s) and -- sorry, (r) and (s) and how it compares to the accuracy of what's in the KLA communique. Is the KLA communique accurate, as far as you know? And can you correct the date to November 1997?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for paragraph (r), it is absolutely accurate as far as dates and information are concerned contained in that paragraph relating to the killing of Dragan Davidovic. As for paragraph (s), the mistake is in November 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The KLA communique, do they accurate reflect, as far as your information says or what was available to you, do they accurately reflect what actually happened? That's communique 40, with the exception of the alleged attack on the Cessna being brought down.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, it does not, because Zarko Milosevic is a close friend of mine, a policeman, and he explained to me and also through the official documents I knew how this event occurred in their public communique, Gjocaj is being presented as a prominent member of the KLA. We did not have information that he was in the KLA. We knew that he was a KLA sympathiser. And in a quite cunning way, he pulled out his gun in the vehicle he was when he was being detained, and due to the lack of attention of the police officers, he killed a policeman, injured or wounded Zarko Milosevic and this, the third one who was there, Lutovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One general question in relation to all these documents. If you give dates in your 92 ter statement, now, usually have you taken them from the documents or do you have any personal recollection of these dates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am speaking on the basis of recollection about the month. But then when I look at the document, then I can give you a precise date. In some situation, I can directly refer to the date or the time frame when this happened. This is something that was clear to remember, because on the same day there was an attack on the police section in Rznic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I then ask you -- one second, please. The -- one of the documents you referred to was about the two attacks: One against Shukri Krasniqi and the other one against Sredoje Radojevic. The other was about the attack on four police posts, and the third event mentioned there was the destruction of three apartments in Babaloc. Now, these three events, as far as the publication of the communiques is concerned, how -- where is your -- your memory serves you in what way in relation to the communiques in relation to these events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The communiques would appear a day or a few days after an incident was carried out. The publication of the communiques in Zeri i Kosoves depends -- it's a paper that is published in Switzerland -- would then depend on its periodical issues. The attack would be carried out on one date and then with the development of the terrorist activities, the KLA after a while was able to publish communiques immediately after an action. Sometimes the communiques would be published a day or two afterwards and subsequently would be then published in Zeri i Kosoves. Later these communiques would be sent out to all the media locally and also internationally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the communiques always followed within, you said, one or two days? Could it be more than one week or -- or were these communiques always within one week of the event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am convinced that three to five days would be the maximum period, according to analysis that would pass from the carried-out event until the publication later. In 1997, 1998, 1999, the taking of responsibility would be done from attack to attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you for the following reason: In your 92 ter statement, under (e), you are referring to three KLA communiques and you say they were all dated the 14th of August. And I wondered what made you accept that events described to have taken place on 7th and 10th of July, the other attack on four police both dated the 2nd of August, and then finally the attack against the apartments in Babaloc taking place on August the 8th, what makes you believe that all these three communiques are dated the 14th of August? I'm -- I was wondering.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember very well this communique and this event. What -- this day when it was published in Zeri i Kosoves, there was a presentation of all -- of the statements 21, 22, and 23 about the attacks that had been executed in that area. They were all dated of the 14th of August -- well, perhaps maybe I made a mistake there. Maybe I was mistaken that this all happened on the same day. If we had communique 21 here, when Radovic was killed, it would be one to five days after the killing of Radovic. In this case, Zeri i Kosoves put together the three communiques and described what had happened on this particular occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm simply looking in this connection at the translation of annex 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which is indeed the translation of the Zeri i Kosoves article in which all three communiques are reported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But not on the 14th but on the 29th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No, Mr. Emmerson, I'm afraid that you're making a mistake. The publication was dated the 29th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But from what I understand, there's no reference to the dates of the communiques --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- covered by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the witness, therefore, when he gives in his statement the 14th of August as the date, I wondered what made him --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- say that they were all on the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas, the other communiques usually are quite separate in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Further, Mr. Re, I have a similar question, then we'll really have the break. In relation to 20(a), could we have that on the screen, that is annex 5, and annex 5 is P937. Could that be on the screen. Oh, it is -- perhaps it is already. Yes. In your -- let me just check that. Yes. Mr. Stijovic, your statement, your 92 ter statement tells us that in June 1995 the police station in Rznic was attacked. I have some difficulties to find support for that in annex 5, which is P -- I think -- could you please have a look at that. P937.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the second paragraph, it says that the command --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the names that were attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you -- could you please repeat it. The interpreters couldn't follow you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness was reading in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please read the -- what you said was the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not in the second paragraph. I am reading -- I have announcement number 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the second paragraph, it says that the police station or command was attacked. The police station of the Serbian police in Rznic was attacked, that an attack was carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when was that carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the same day when the Davidovic, Plutov [as interpreted] and Milosevic incident occurred. That attack, which was carried out in Rznic, in the radio communications there was a certain lack of care or attention by the security officials who were driving these people who had committed this incident in the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My problem is the following: That in your statement, you say this happened in June 1995. However, in my translation of the communique number 13, the attack on the police station at Rznic - and that seems to be in accordance with some other evidence we heard - took place in April. Is that -- and not in June. Although, the communique dates from June, but it doesn't ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's absolutely certain that the police section in Rznic was frequently exposed to attacks. And there was an attack in April in the village of Rznic. This is correct. This can be checked in the documents of the public security -- or the SUP of Decani. It is also correct that that day when Davidovic was killed in the vehicle and when Lutovac and Milosevic were wounded, that day at that point in time an attack was carried out on the police section in Rznic. And what they heard on the communication system was the call for assistance from the police station in Rznic, which led to a moment of inattention, which the person they were driving used, pulled the gun from -- off from one of the police officers, killed Davidovic, wounded the other two, and after that in the mutual exchange of fire he was killed as well. So at the point in time when the Rznic section was attacked and a call for assistance was issued, Mehe used that moment of inattention and carried out his attack. But I didn't go in to checking exactly how many attacks there were at that time. This is something that can be checked. Ultimately, the police withdrew from that particular section and left that police station without any staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember when that happened, that they withdrew? Without leaving any staff behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very soon after the events of March 1998 or after the conflict of the 24th of March in Glodjane, when policeman Otovic was killed, not long after that time the police withdrew from Rznic, because as I said, that police department was exposed to constant attacks, bomb attacks, sniper fire, attacks from automatic weapons. And in my view, then an erroneous decision was made from the police administration to pull out and relocate the police staff from Rznic to Decan, and in the end the police carried out their activities by stepping up the numbers of police groups that were patrolling that area. The building itself was abandoned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And -- and now, it's not entirely clear to me. You referred also to what happened in June. Was there then another attack on the police -- on the police command post in Rznic in June or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In June and in April. And, Your Honours, I can state with full responsibility that those attacks were so frequent that it would be very important for you perhaps to get that list attacks and the effects of the attacks that were going on there. The Rznic police station was a constant target just as the Klincina station was and Celopek. These places were constantly under attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I might have been confused with the last question, is that, of course, is all 1995 and not 1998. Thank you for reminding me that it was 1995. We'll have a break until 4.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, before the break you were looking at annex 21, which is MFI P953. I just want to alert the Trial Chamber to the fact that that is referred to in annex -- or cross-referenced to annex 5 of Mr. Jakup Krasniqi's 92 ter statement, which is P328. And the reference there is publication in a -- have I got the right one? Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, the next thing I want to take you to is: In paragraph 20(k), you referred to the death of Ali Qullapeku, and you say in the 1940s and 1950s he had been an informer for the DB. Now, the KLA assumed responsibility for killing him in its communique number 35 of 5th of August, 1997, which is annex 16 to your statement, which is MFI P948. I just want you to briefly tell the Trial Chamber what you mean there when you say that he was an informer in the 1940s and 1950s.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an active associate of the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, how well known was that to the people in the village of Tertenik, near Glogovac, where he lived?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the village is Trstenik. Maybe there's a mistake in the translation, Tertenik. In the early 1980s and 1990s when the political turbulence in Kosovo and Metohija began and when the significant number of people on the call of the Democratic alliance of Kosovo left the institutions of the system, following that appeal a number of State Security employees also left. From the start of the 1990s, it was known in the broader area where he was that he was an associate in the earlier period of the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And in the communique number 35, which is on the screen, which is MFI P948, it says: "Prior to this, our guerilla units took care of the assassination of Ali Qullapeku from Trsteniku [phoen] and Ramiz Luku from Bajiqa [phoen] of Gllogovcu [phoen] motivated by the anti-nationalist activity." Where it says took care of the assassination, what did these guerilla units actually do? What was your information about what they did?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Qullopeku was of an age where nobody could do anything in that period. He was an elderly man of poor material status.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's in the statement. I'm actually asking you what they did to him.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ali Qullopeku was killed in the village where he lived. He was killed by members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that is also cross-referenced to annex 2 of Jakup Krasniqi's 92 ter statement, Exhibit P328. Paragraph 21 of your statement. Can we please go to that now. The Trial Chamber has decided not to admit the statement in that form. You said -- you referred to use of the term "sabotage and terrorist group." I want you to elaborate what was meant by the term "sabotage and terrorist group" and who used it and in what context.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the initial development of terrorist activities of the KLA, the qualification of somebody who executed those terrorist attacks was that this was committed by sabotage and terrorist groups. The name was, first of all, related to the careerism in the power hierarchy and nonacceptance of the need to call things by their proper name, to call a spade a spade. In that period, when the term was used in communications and information in the DB, already at that time it was a quite clearly pronounced organised terrorist organisation. That was a period of terrorism. And after that, the escalating terrorist activity led to armed uprising in 1998. I think that the political and the police leadership - and I mentioned why it was the police leadership - unnecessarily minimised the degree and level of danger that the KLA presented for Yugoslavia. And this contributed to an inadequate and late adoption of decisions of the state leadership to combat those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just in relation to the term "sabotage and terrorist group," what is that in Serbian? Just say the words.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Diverzantsko-teroristicka grupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was that abbreviated to DTG?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When documents refer to DTG - that's the documents annexed to your statement and other documents emanating from Serbian official archives for that period - is that referring to the KLA or something else?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA. And the term DTG is erroneously used. In analysis -- we in analysis did not use that term. The information that we received from the field, the reports, we would collate them. And in our reporting, we would use the term "so-called Liberation Army of Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if you turn to annex 23 in your pile of documents, which is MFI P955, which is an information from the Deputy Federal Minister of Foreign Affairs in relation to the correct descriptions of the operations of -- by the Ministry of Interior organs in Kosovo-Metohija dated the 16th of March, 1998. I want you to turn to the information where it says: "We believe that the operations by organs of the MUP cannot be described as an internal armed conflict in the sense of Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions. This concerns a police action directed at preventing crimes, acts of terrorism. It's a very important distinction. To describe the aforementioned incidents as an internal armed conflict could be interpreted as an implicit recognition of the so-called KLA as a warring side, which would also have certain international legal implications. This is also significant in order to determine any possible jurisdiction of the International Criminal Tribunal at The Hague, which is responsible exclusively for crimes committed in internal -- international internal conflicts with the exception of genocide." Then proposing you don't use the word armed conflict but to speak of the operation by the MUP to prevent crimes. I'm just paraphrasing that. Was this a document -- or how widely distributed was this document, to your knowledge? And what was its nature?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see this document, but the document was not broadly distributed. It was sent to the leadership in the state and the public security service, and they sent out information to lower units about actions and the use of terminology relating to that. It's actually what I said, they did not deal with the essence and the actual facts on the ground of what was happening. It was more a matter of form and minimising everything that was happening, which in turn led to everything that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You just a moment ago referred to the use of "DTG" instead of "KLA." How does this particular document disseminated by the Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs fit in with the use of the term "DTJ" instead of -- "DTG" instead of "KLA"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does fit in in the sense that this document, as far as I understood - it's from March 1998 - and in March 1998 it talks about acts of terrorism. In March of 1998 in Kosovo and Metohija, actually what was happening was the beginning of armed uprising. So again we have this minimising of the actual situation on the ground because of some other interests. You've read the reasons why this was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you base your view you just expressed there on, where you say that March 1998 was the beginning of armed uprising?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that because as of March, their activities escalated. The political activities of the Albanian political parties were there for the purpose of the NPK. In the field, it specifically meant the merging of Albanian parties, the Democratic League of Kosovo, the parliamentary parties of Albanians and the rest within the structures of the KLA in order to assume control of large parts of territory in Kosovo. This was followed by interrupting regular communication by using roads in Kosovo and Metohija. We can say that as early as March the road between Pec and Pristina, which was of strategic importance for Serbia, was completely insecure for any movement, to be civilian or military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. If I might. To the extent the gentleman is -- is interposing an opinion at this point, with regard to the issue of an armed uprising, I would object. He's not being offered as an expert witness and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, he wasn't asked. I think, as a matter of fact, he was asked what was the basis for a certain view, and then I understand that Mr. Re was seeking factual basis for his --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear that we have here a bit of a mixture.
